meal.name: Coq au Vin Dinner — Skinless Thighs, Oven Braise
meal.workflow_md:
# Meal Workflow
**Critical path:** braise is the long pole; strategy = early completion + safe hold. Into oven T-140; tenderness gate window T-95 to T-65; sauce finished at exit; chicken held in sauce at 170°F / 77°C until T-12 reheat on Induction A, which governs plating.
**Failure priority:** protect chicken tenderness endpoint. Do not serve under-tender thighs — service slides; purée holds in Tiger, croutons on rack, beans dressed only once new service time is fixed.
**Oven:** preheat 300°F at T-160 (\~15 min). Braise T-140 → gate. At exit, door open \~2 min, reset to 170°F hold (gated on sauce temp at T-12, not dial). No other oven use.
**Heat allocation:**
- Induction A: lardons/brown/aromatics T-195 to T-140 → sauce finish at braise exit (15 min) → reheat T-12 to T-3.
- Induction B: wine reduction T-180 to T-160 → beans T-130 to T-115 → onions then mushrooms T-110 to T-82 → potatoes T-80 to T-45 → lardon re-crisp + croutons T-35 to T-28.
- Outdoor gas: overflow only.
- Flambé: Induction B saucepan clear, extractor off.
**Band closure:** earliest exit T-95 → sauce done T-80 → hold 68 min (≤75 planned ceiling ✓). Latest exit T-65 → sauce done T-50 → hold 38 min ✓. Beyond band: 10-min checks to T-35 max; after that service slides.
# T-minus Timeline
- Sunday 8:00–10:00 am: skin thighs; salt 9 g / 3 tsp Diamond Crystal; uncovered on rack, fridge (≥5 h before browning).
- T-200: prep — dice onion, carrot, lardons; slice half mushrooms, quarter half; mince garlic; chop thyme, parsley; measure 710 ml wine, 30 ml brandy; thaw frozen pearl onions in sieve.
- T-195: Induction A — render lardons medium-low 10–15 min until golden-crisp. Fat stays in pot. Half lardons → braise; half → fridge (garnish).
- T-180: Induction B — 710 ml / 3 cups wine to boil (15–20 min). Induction A — pat thighs dry, brown batch 1 (3–4 min/side).
- T-172 / T-164: batches 2 and 3.
- T-160: preheat oven 300°F / 150°C. Wine into jug — off heat at 355 ml / 1½ cups (top up with water if under).
- T-155: pour off fat if \>2 tbsp. Onion, carrot, sliced mushrooms, ¼ tsp salt — 8 min, scraping fond.
- T-147: garlic, tomato paste, thyme 1 min; flour 1 min.
- T-145: flambé brandy off heat. Add reduced wine, scrape. Return chicken + juices, braise lardons, bay. Simmer, cover.
- T-140: into oven.
- T-130: Induction B — salted water to boil.
- T-122: blanch beans 3–4 min; ice bath 2 min; dry; fridge.
- T-120: 20-min bubbling check; turn thighs. Dead still → raise to 325°F / 163°C.
- T-110: Induction B — pearl onions covered low 15 min.
- T-95: onions uncovered medium-high 3–5 min to burnish; remove. First tenderness gate.
- T-95 to T-65 (at gate pass): thighs to covered dish back in oven; oven → 170°F / 77°C. Skim; reduce sauce on A to nappe 10–15 min; first salt pass slightly under; vinegar reserved. Chicken back in pot, covered, oven hold (planned max 75 min).
- T-90: Induction B — mushrooms medium-high 5–8 min; salt; combine with onions, uncovered, room temp.
- T-80: Induction B — potatoes into cold salted water.
- T-50 to T-45: potato gate; drain; steam-dry 1 min.
- T-45: rice; butter; warm milk. Into Tiger keep-warm by T-38 (planned max 60 min).
- T-35: Induction B — re-crisp garnish lardons 1–2 min, reserve. Croutons 2 min/side; salt; rack uncovered.
- T-30: beans out of fridge; whisk vinaigrette.
- T-12: pot to Induction A; add onions + mushrooms; gentle simmer 5–7 min, basting. Loosen with 1–2 tbsp water if tightened. Sauce ≥165°F / 74°C.
- T-8: final taste — salt, then vinegar ¼ tsp at a time (max 2 tsp).
- T-5: dress beans.
- T-4: purée check; loosen with warm milk.
- T-3: plate ×3 — purée, 2 thighs, sauce + onions + mushrooms, lardons, parsley, croutons dry on top, beans alongside.
- T-0: serve.
*Plating window: croutons fail first — plate them last, never into sauce.*
# Holding Chain
- Braise — pot covered, oven 170°F / 77°C — max 75 min (planned). Drift: sauce tightens → 1–2 tbsp water at T-12; meat keeps softening → pull at first passing gate.
- Reduced wine — saucepan off heat — 20 min.
- Onions + mushrooms — bowl uncovered, room temp — 90 min. Soften → reheated in sauce at T-12.
- Garnish lardons — fridge until T-35. Soft → re-crisp.
- Beans — fridge, undressed — 2 h. Vinegar greys them → dress at T-5 only.
- Purée — Tiger keep-warm — 60 min (planned). Stiffens → warm milk 1 tbsp at a time.
- Croutons — rack uncovered — 30 min. Humidity → re-toast 30 s.
**Meal balance:** richness stacks (lardons, butter, purée, croutons) → relieved by beans/vinaigrette. Acid roles distinct: wine = depth, vinegar = conditional correction, vinaigrette = reset. Temperature: hot braise/purée vs room-temp beans. Texture: tender meat, napping sauce, crisp croutons/lardons, snapping beans, smooth purée. No chilli.

# Shared Prep
- Butter: 92 g / 6½ tbsp — 42 g / 3 tbsp coq (14 g onions, 28 g croutons), 50 g / 3½ tbsp purée.
- Red wine vinegar: 4 tsp — 2 tsp vinaigrette, up to 2 tsp coq reserve.
- Extra-virgin olive oil: 6 tbsp / 80 g — 4 tbsp coq (1 browning reserve, 1 onions, 1 mushrooms, 1 croutons), 2 tbsp vinaigrette.
meal.wine_pairing: Wine pairing (when requested): Dijon vinaigrette is the component that fights red Burgundy — keep it at 1:3 vinegar to oil; don't sharpen it.

dishes.summary: Skinless bone-in thighs gently braised in reduced Pinot on a lardon-fat mirepoix base — thighs tender but intact, sauce that naps, with dry croutons, re-crisped lardons, burnished pearl onions and browned mushrooms.
dishes.method_md:
# Design decisions (vs NYT original)
- Skin removed before cooking and discarded — braised skin = flabby (Core hard failure). Skinless thighs brown the meat itself and render less fat.
- Wine marinade dropped — wine barely penetrates, and wine-stained surface browns poorly. Dry-brine instead; wine goes straight to reduction. Design choice, not an open test.
- Wine reduced in a separate saucepan (Induction B) during browning; endpoint 355 ml by measuring jug, not time.
- Flour kept at 1 tbsp for first cook; test 2 tsp later only if sauce naps well but reads flour-muted.
- Oven braise 300°F / 150°C with bubbling gate and 325°F / 163°C contingency; tenderness gate replaces fixed 60 min.
- Early completion + hot hold (Meal Workflow long-cook strategy).
- Onions and mushrooms cooked sequentially in the same skillet (not crowded together).
- Croutons served dry — never dipped. Half the lardons re-crisped for garnish.
- Finishing acid = red wine vinegar in ¼-tsp steps, conditional.
- Pot: narrow oval Le Creuset 27.5 × 21.5 × 10.5 cm — 6 thighs in one snug layer; brown in 3 batches of 2; liquid expected ≈ top of thighs.
# 1. Coq au Vin
*Serves 3 (2 thighs each) · \~3 h 20 min day-of + morning salting · Active \~75 min · Oven 300°F / 150°C · Braise band 45–75 min (designed)*
**Overview.** Skinless thighs gently braised in reduced Pinot on a lardon-fat mirepoix base. Target: thighs tender but intact, sauce that naps. Crunch from dry croutons and re-crisped lardons; bite from burnished pearl onions and browned mushrooms.
**Ingredients**
- 6 bone-in chicken thighs, \~3¼ lb / 1.45 kg skin-on (\~1.2 kg skinned)
- 9 g / 3 tsp Diamond Crystal (0.75% skinned weight) + ¼ tsp for vegetables
- ½ tsp black pepper
- 4 oz / 115 g lardons, ¼ in / 6 mm dice
- 1 large onion, diced
- 1 large carrot, peeled and diced
- 8 oz / 225 g mushrooms — 4 oz / 115 g sliced (base), 4 oz / 115 g quartered (garnish)
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp tomato paste
- 1 tsp chopped thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tbsp / 8 g all-purpose flour
- 2 tbsp / 30 ml brandy
- 710 ml / 3 cups Pinot Noir → reduced to 355 ml / 1½ cups
- Up to 2 tsp red wine vinegar (reserve)
- 8 oz / 225 g pearl onions + pinch sugar
- 3 tbsp / 42 g unsalted butter
- 4 tbsp / 55 g extra-virgin olive oil
- 2 slices white bread, crusts off, each cut in 4 triangles
- ¼ cup / 15 g chopped parsley
**Flavor architecture.** Base: lardon fat; onion, carrot, sliced mushroom, garlic, tomato paste. Primary driver: reduced red wine + chicken juices. Acid: wine (early, structural) + vinegar (late, conditional, tasted at T-8 with garnish in). Finish: pearl onions, browned mushrooms, crisp lardons, parsley, dry croutons. Tomato paste and brandy held at original amounts.
**Prep.** Skin thighs; discard skins. Salt morning-of, uncovered on rack in fridge — surface tacky-dry; pat any beads. Pot: narrow oval Le Creuset.
**Active cooking**
- Lardons: medium-low 10–15 min, golden-crisp. Split half/half.
- Browning: lardon fat, medium, until shimmering. 3 batches of 2, 3–4 min/side — done when the side releases without tearing and is deep golden. Oil (1 tbsp) only if dry.
- Wine reduction: saucepan, Induction B, parallel. Endpoint 355 ml by jug.
- Aromatics: onion, carrot, sliced mushrooms, ¼ tsp salt — 8 min medium, scraping. Garlic, paste, thyme 1 min; flour 1 min.
- Flambé: off heat, extractor off, brandy from a measure into cleared space, long lighter, lid within reach. Alternative: cook down 1 min.
- Braise: add wine, scrape; return thighs + juices, braise lardons, bay; simmer; cover; oven 300°F. At 20 min: occasional lazy bubbles expected — turn thighs; if dead still, raise to 325°F. Expected liquid ≈ top of thighs (record on the day).
- Doneness gate (submerged to service — no formal rest): from 45 min, every 10 min. Primary cue — thin probe into thickest meat beside (not touching) bone enters with little resistance → done; grips → continue. Secondary — thigh lifts whole on slotted spoon; meat sliding off bone = past target. Safety floor ≥165°F / 74°C throughout (far exceeded at tenderness endpoint).
- Sauce finish: lift thighs; tilt and skim; reduce medium-high to nappe (coats spoon; finger line holds). Salt slightly under; hold vinegar. Return chicken; hold.
- Garnish (Induction B): pearl onions — 1 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp oil, sugar, pinch salt; covered low 15 min, shaking; uncovered medium-high 3–5 min until burnished and knife enters easily but shape holds. Mushrooms — 1 tbsp oil, medium-high; undisturbed 3 min, 5–8 min total until cut faces brown; salt at end.
**Holding & assembly.** T-12: garnish into pot, gentle simmer to ≥165°F. T-8: final taste — salt, then vinegar ¼ tsp at a time. Croutons: re-crisp garnish lardons in skillet first (their fat seasons the bread), then 2 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp oil medium until bubbling; triangles \~2 min/side golden; salt; rack. Plate: thigh on purée, sauce and garnish over, lardons and parsley scattered, croutons dry on top.
**Critical control points**
1. Major (b) — Chicken steams instead of browning: surface stays grey, wet, sticks and tears. Unrecoverable for sear depth; dish serviceable. Prevent: dry surface, 3 batches.
2. Major (a) — Fond scorches during aromatics: black spots, acrid smell before deglaze. Recovery: transfer to a clean pot before wine; accept shallower fond.
3. Major (b) — Braise overshoots: meat slides off bone on lift. Unrecoverable for whole-thigh presentation; dish serviceable. Prevent: pull at first passing gate.
4. Major (a) — Sauce thin or greasy at T-8: runs off spoon, fat pools. Recovery: skim; reduce with chicken lifted out.
**Adjustment notes.** Salt — finishing salt on the chicken at the table. Acid — drops of vinegar into an individual portion. Richness — more parsley, bigger bean portion.
**Scaling.** Narrow pot max \~7 thighs single layer; beyond → wide Le Creuset, recheck liquid depth, may need more wine. Browning batches scale linearly. Wine reduction time non-linear — keep the jug.

dishes.name: Pommes Purée
dishes.source: Adapted from Melissa Clark, NYT Cooking ([cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1018529-coq-au-vin](http://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1018529-coq-au-vin)). Rebuilt under governance v3.5 (2026-07-20); Claude build, GPT cross-checked and reconciled 29 Sep 2026.
dishes.summary: Smooth, loose, neutral riced-potato purée with butter and warm milk — the carrier for the coq au vin sauce.
dishes.method_md:
# 2. Pommes Purée
*Serves 3 (Lukas full, adults small) · \~45 min · Active \~15 min*
- Overview: smooth, loose, neutral carrier for the sauce. Meal-level texture exemption — purée inherently single-texture; contrast from croutons, lardons, beans.
- Ingredients: 1 lb 2 oz / 500 g Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled, 1¼ in / 3 cm chunks; 50 g / 3½ tbsp unsalted butter, cubed; 120 ml / ½ cup whole milk, warm, + 60 ml / ¼ cup for loosening; 1% salted water (\~15 g Diamond Crystal per 1.5 L).
- Flavor architecture: base butter + milk; primary potato; acid none; finish none.
- Method: cold-water start. Simmer 18–22 min — knife meets no resistance at centre → drain; grips → 3 more min. Steam-dry 1 min. Rice hot; fold in butter, then milk. No blender or processor.
- Holding: Tiger keep-warm (planned max 60 min); loosen at T-4 with warm milk.
- CCP: Major (b) — gluey, stretchy from overworking. Unrecoverable for texture; dish serviceable.
- Adjustment: salt at table. Scaling: N/A.

dishes.summary: Snapping blanched haricots verts in a mild Dijon–red wine vinaigrette, served at room temperature as the meal's crisp-fresh counterweight.
dishes.method_md:
# 3. Haricots Verts, Dijon–Red Wine Vinaigrette
*Serves 3 · \~15 min + fridge hold · Active \~10 min*
- Overview: snapping beans, mild mustard vinaigrette, room temperature — the meal's crisp-fresh counterweight. Meal-level carve-out: provides the meal's crisp-fresh contrast; no internal contrast required.
- Ingredients: 9 oz / 250 g haricots verts, trimmed; 1 tsp Dijon; 2 tsp red wine vinegar; 2 tbsp / 25 g extra-virgin olive oil; ¼ tsp Diamond Crystal; pepper.
- Flavor architecture: base olive oil; primary Dijon; acid vinegar (added at T-5 only — holding greys the beans); finish pepper.
- Method: blanch in 1% salted boiling water 3–4 min. Taste one — bends with a clean snap and no squeak → shock; squeaks → 30 s more. Ice bath 2 min; dry thoroughly.
- Holding: fridge undressed; out at T-30; dress T-5.
- CCP: Major (b) — overcooked, olive-drab, limp. Unrecoverable for snap; dish serviceable.
- Adjustment: drop more vinegar if flat against the sauce. Scaling: N/A.
